Posted November 6, 2000
(MarijuanaNews note: I am going over a week early – leaving on Friday, November 10th, to interview my Dutch anti-prohibitionist friends. I am looking forward to seeing friends from around the world… and whatever else I may find in Amsterdam.)

For Immediate Release

Cannabis Cup 2000 to highlight The Goddess, featuring Patti Smith, Galactic, Jefferson Starship and others in Amsterdam Nov. 19-23


The 13th Annual High Times Cannabis Cup—the world championship of marijuana—will take place in Amsterdam Nov. 19-23, with special emphasis on women’s contributions to the culture of cannabis. The " Goddess Cup " will feature world-class entertainment, the Cannabis Castaways, a host of female marijuana celebrities, an extensive vendor Expo, bus tours of Amsterdam’s finest coffeeshops, and cutting-edge seminars and workshops. Two thousand judges from America and around the world are expected to attend and vote in
10 categories.

" We have specifically chosen the goddess as our theme because we feel that the goddess promotes peace and healing to all of humanity, " explains Michael Esterson, president of 420 Tours, organizers of the Cannabis Cup. " The plant is a female, the Earth is a mother, lets learn to respect her. "

Legendary punk rocker Patti Smith, the one and only Jefferson Starship featuring Paul Kantner and Marty Balin, and New Orleans psychedelic jazz jammers Galactic will continue the Cup tradition of presenting top-notch music. In addition to the headliners, performers at Amsterdam’s renowned Melkweg entertainment complex include Comedy Central’s award-winning Upright Citizen’s Brigade, Canadian Comedienne MC Watermelon, DJ Rocker-T and Robin Ludwig’s Five Points Band.

The Pax Party House will once again host the Expo and seminars by top marijuana experts, as well as panels and workshops featuring America’s leading women marijuana activists.

This year, the Cannabis Cup itself will be chosen by the Cannabis Castaways, a group of two women and four men specially selected from a pool of over 100 applicants who each sent in a video to convince the organizers why they should be chosen to judge the top prize. Katie, DJ Nitro, Amie, Jeff, Jet, and Dan will be stranded on an Amsterdam houseboat for three days with " unprecedented access to the world’s best cannabis, " according to Esterson.

Numbered strains of cannabis will be smoked and eliminated as the Castaways, isolated and under constant video surveillance, have the enviable mission of smoking through 20 varieties until a clear winner emerges from the haze. At the Melkweg, Cup judges will be treated to nightly video episodes of the Castaways’ daily activites, which promise to be quite entertaining. At the Awards Ceremony on Thursday, Nov. 23 the winners of the Cannabis Cup, Peoples’ Cup, and the eight other Cups will be revealed.

Ina May Gaskin, author of Spiritual Midwifery and founder of the modern midwifery movement, will be inducted into the Counterculture Hall of Fame this year, the first woman to be so honored. She will join previous inductees Bob Marley, Allen Ginsberg, William Burroughs, Neal Cassady, Jack Kerouac, Mezz Mezzrow and Louis Armstrong for her outstanding contributions to the culture.

The annual Hemp Fashion Show will take place at the Awards Ceremony on Tuesday evening, November 21st at the Melkweg. The groundbreaking 1996 High Times Cannabis Cup Fashion Show helped transform a potato-sack industry into a full-fledged fashion aesthetic recognized around the world, and this year’s event promises to continue this tradition of excellence, featuring outrageous and functional hemp apparel from Europe, the US and Asia.

The Cannabis Cup is the world’s leading convention for marijuana lovers and connoisseurs, and provides a forum in the liberal city of Amsterdam, The Netherlands for experts and activists to share ideas concerning cultivation, breeding, and legal issues. The tremendous abuses of the American and worldwide Drug War have focused this year’s seminars on activism and education. " We have more than two million people in jail, " says Steven Hager, High Times Editor-in-Chief. " Our country doesn't build hospitals, doesn't
build schools and doesn't build day-care centers. It builds prisons. This is not the hallmark of a free society, but of a police state. "

This year a distinguished Cup panel of female activists has been convened by America’s most respected marijuana legalization group, the National Organization for the Reform of Marijuana Laws (NORML).

Panel seminars include " The Impact of Marijuana Prohibition on Civil Liberties, Families and Racial Minorities, " led by attorney Deborah Small (an expert on race and the American Drug War), with attorney Nancy Lord Johnson (an expert on FDA and international law), Monica Pratt (Communications Director of Families against
Mandatory Minimums) and Mikki Norris (who will talk about families shattered by the Drug War); " Patients and Patient Cooperatives, " led by Hilary Black (founder of Canada’s BC Compassion Club), with Valerie Corral (a California medical marijuana patient and grower) and Kitty Tucker (an attorney and patient fighting for medical marijuana in Maryland, busted by police for growing a small medical garden); and " Grass-Roots Organizing, Voter Initiatives and Public Education, " led by Debby Goldsberry (National Director of the Cannabis Action Network), with Elvy Musikka (a continuing recipient of US government medical marijuana), Dominic Holden (of the Hemp Coalition) and Wiccan marijuana activist Miriam White. Other noted panelists include Toni Leeman (of Floridians for Medical Rights) and Sandee Burbank (Director of Mothers Against Misuse and Abuse).

NORML National Director Keith Stroup will be on hand to host the seminars.
